html:
The Jakaltek, who call their language Popti', are a Maya people of the highlands of northwestern Guatemala, around Jacaltenango in Huehuetenango, and of nearby Chiapas in Mexico. Their language belongs to the Q'anjob'alan branch of the Mayan family, close to that of the Q'anjob'al.

Like other highland Maya (Maya) they farm maize and beans and keep their own customs and calendar knowledge. During Guatemala's civil war, army massacres in the early 1980s drove many Jakaltek across the border into Mexico as refugees. The Jakaltek writer Víctor Montejo described the destruction of one village in his book "Testimony". Their neighbours include the Chuj.
